deep.reconstruction:
Context: section B of the 1983 Teichmüller notes. These notes set up a category (written SCD^+ on the previous page) of objects (X, Σ, R). X is a surface, Σ a family of distinguished circles (contours/cutting circles indexed by a set A), and R a 'marking', meaning a finite set of marked points on some of the circles. The previous page defined two operations: weakening a marking (forgetting points) and 'surmarquage' (over-marking: adding r'(b) new subdivision vertices on each open arc). The next page treats cutting along circles (C), as opposed to 'gommage', which contracts a circle to a point.

This page restricts attention, 'pour les besoins pratiques', to special 'uniform' operations. Their effect is read off on each circle a ∈ A. The marked points R_a on circle a form a torsor under the cyclic group Z_a/r(a), where Z_a = Z ∧^{±1} ω(a) is Z twisted by the orientation torsor ω(a) of the circle. A choice of orientation identifies Z_a with Z, and the generator is rotation to the next marked point.

Two operations are defined:
(i) Partial uniform erasure ('gommage partiel uniforme en a'), for r'(a) | r(a). The torsor under Z_a/r(a) is turned into a torsor under Z_a/r'(a). Canonically this is extension of structure group along the quotient map Z/r → Z/r': the torsor R_a is replaced by R_a/(r'Z/rZ), i.e. marked points are identified modulo rotation by r' steps. Geometrically, one keeps every (r/r')-th point up to the choice of the residue class.
(ii) Uniform over-marking of multiplier d(a) ('surmarquage uniforme'). Here r''(a) = d(a) r(a), and a Z/r-torsor is lifted to a Z/dr-torsor, i.e. d(a)-1 new points are inserted on each arc.

Grothendieck then remarks that partial erasure is in fact a weakening (forgetting) of structure. Conversely, uniform over-markings are a strengthening of structure: combinatorially they require extra data, namely the choice of the multipliers d(a), plus the lift. The purpose is to have a manageable class of functorial operations relating the discrete combinatorial models (graphs with marked contours) used to build the Teichmüller tower/groupoids at varying marking levels.
errors: Grothendieck's wording calls passing from Z_a/r(a) to Z_a/r'(a) (r'|r) a 'restriction' of the operator group and passing to Z_a/r''(a) an 'extension'. Strictly, Z/r' is a quotient of Z/r, so the canonical (forgetful) operation is pushing the torsor forward along Z/r → Z/r'. Lifting to Z/dr requires a choice. The sentence ending the page partly corrects this by noting that the gommage is a weakening and the surmarquage a strengthening of structure.

The lifted Z/dr-torsor in a surmarquage is not canonical; the set of lifts has its own torsor structure. Like the previous page ('il y a des choix arbitraires'), the page leaves this non-canonicity implicit, saying only that the result is defined up to unique isomorphism once the new marked set is retained.

ideas.what: Encoding the marked points on an oriented-up-to-sign boundary circle as a torsor under Z/r twisted by the orientation torsor (Z ∧^{±1} ω(a))
ideas.modern_name: cyclic torsor of boundary marked points; twisted cyclic group / orientation local system
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (ribbon graphs, marked bordered surfaces: Penner, Kontsevich, Fomin–Shapiro–Thurston)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses Teichmüller tower and Lego with marked surfaces, but not this torsor formalism explicitly

ideas.what: Uniform partial erasure (quotient Z/r → Z/r', r'|r) and uniform over-marking with multiplier d (Z/dr → Z/r) as change-of-structure-group operations on marking torsors
ideas.modern_name: change of structure group for torsors; refinement/coarsening of boundary marked points

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but routine bookkeeping step in setting up the combinatorial category of marked surfaces for the Teichmüller tower. The torsor-under-twisted-cyclic-group formalism is elegant, but it is standard and leads to no new result.
transcription_corrections: 'géométrie partielle' should read 'gommage partiel' (erasure/contraction, cf. 'gommer' on the next page).
'opérations de géométrie par des régions' likely reads 'opérations de gommage par régions' (or similar).
'affaiblissement de structure, par une renforcement' likely reads 'un affaiblissement de structure, pas un renforcement'.
Formula line: Z_a = Z ∧^{±1} ω(a), i.e. Z twisted by the orientation torsor via {±1}, with a crossed-out earlier attempt 'Z_a(r(a))'.
First line likely 'On va peut-être se borner pour les besoins pratiques...'.
Marginal insertion above 'gommage partiel' reads 'uniforme' (doubly underlined).
